results.title: AI Monetization Requires a New Billing Infrastructure Layer | Vijayanand Kailash posted on the topic | LinkedIn
results.content: customer still expects one simple experience.That's where I think a new layer is emerging in the AI stack. Not another payment processor. Not another invoicing tool. But a billing infrastructure layer that understands how an AI product actually creates value and incurs cost. Many AI companies are going to end up building this as an internal microservice: Track events → calculate usage → apply pricing rules → calculate cost → add margin → deduct credits → enforce limits → send the final amount to the payment system. That's a lot of billing logic to build and maintain. This is exactly the microservice we are replacing with Clocknext. AI has changed the economics of software. The billing layer needs to change with it. [...] itself feels backwards. Instead, every AI product should have an Incubation stage. - Give the agent real work. - Let it prove its capability. - Measure the outcomes. - Then ask the customer to pay. In the coming years, I wouldn't be surprised if pricing pages looked like this: "Incubator" → Paid Because in the age of AI agents, proof should come before pricing. [...] from the same account → more engagement. Now you have actual intent. That’s when your email lands. That’s when your call converts. That’s when a meeting almost feels… easy. Outbound isn’t broken. We’re just solving the wrong problem.
